introduction: The readings begin inside a family, with the rights of each member and the tenderness of a father for a small child, pass to what parents owe in example and education, and dwell longest on what children owe: a regard for parents set next after the recognition of God. They end with youth, whose strength is asked for the service of a wider community. Honour for parents is common ground among the scriptures and Confucius, and so are its hard cases: the parent who is unjust, the call that divides a household, the child who must become someone else’s parent. Those are the companions gathered here.
questions: The Qur’an, Exodus and Confucius all command honour for parents. What does each add about the spirit in which it is to be given?
The readings say parents are to be obeyed unless they keep one from God. How do the Qur’an and the hard sayings of Jesus draw the same line, and where do they put it?
Gibran says that children “belong not to you”, and Hannah lends her son to the Lord. What do the readings ask parents to give up?
Paul tells Timothy to let no one despise his youth; Bacon thinks young men fitter to invent than to judge. What do the readings on youth expect, and what do they guard against?
Lear calls a thankless child sharper than a serpent’s tooth. What do the readings ask of a child whose parent has been unjust?

outside.why: The rights of son, father and mother must none of them be transgressed, “none of them must be arbitrary”. Paul, having told children to obey, turns to fathers: provoke not your children to wrath.
A small son creeping into his father’s bed at midnight. The psalm takes a father’s tenderness as the nearest likeness of God’s: like as a father pitieth his children.
Bacon, who had no children, saw what the memory shows: the joys of parents are secret, and so are their griefs and fears; children sweeten labours, but they make misfortunes more bitter.
“The most precious of all beings is a loving father and a kind mother.” Proverbs: children’s children are the crown of old men, and the glory of children are their fathers.
A father, far away, is “intimately engaged in remembrance” of his son. The father in the parable watched the road: when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran.

“There is nothing sweeter than that sons may become the spiritual lights of their father.” The Elder who wrote the third letter of John says it of his children in faith: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
Husband and wife are to be as two birds on one branch. Gibran’s counsel on marriage keeps a space in the picture: stand together yet not too near together, for the pillars of the temple stand apart.
“A home without children is like a home without light.” The psalm: lo, children are an heritage of the Lord; as arrows are in the hand of a mighty man, so are children of the youth.
Parents are to be “noble examples” in word and deed. Paul traces Timothy’s faith to two such examples: it dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice.

Parents “must teach their children the laws of life”. Deuteronomy makes the home the school: thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house.
All lasting reform “must commence with the family”. Proverbs gives the reason in a sentence: train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

Every father is charged with the instruction of son and daughter. Proverbs speaks from the child’s side, and names both teachers: hear the instruction of thy father, and forsake not the law of thy mother.

If the mother has learning, her children will be fostered in all excellence. Mary Wollstonecraft argued the same connection in 1792: strengthen the female mind by enlarging it, and there will be an end to blind obedience.
“Education and refinement after maturity becomes extremely difficult.” Plato: the beginning is the most important part of any work, especially in the case of a young and tender thing.
Train thy son that he may “become a true servant of God”. Hannah, bringing the child she had prayed for to the temple: as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord.

A child who sees he is loved for his good qualities will strive for them. Gibran loosens the parents’ hold altogether: your children are not your children; they come through you but not from you. How much of a child’s character is the parents’ to shape?

Parents must strive for the religion of their children, since a child who leaves it will not act as they wish. Jesus foresaw households in which faith itself would divide: he that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me. What should parents who strive “diligently” do when a child’s conscience leads elsewhere?
The verse the reading quotes: serve God, ascribe no thing as partner unto Him, show kindness unto parents. The Qur’an sets the two duties side by side with nothing between.
Regard for parents “hath been mentioned in all the heavenly Books”. At Sinai it is the first commandment after those that concern God: honour thy father and thy mother.
He “hath joined their rights with the rights of His Divinity”. The Qur’an joins them in one clause of thanks: give thanks unto Me and unto thy parents.

The age of maturity is fifteen, and regard for parents remains the greatest of the fruits. Jesus at twelve stays behind in the temple, about his Father’s business, and then goes home with his parents and is subject unto them.
Given a choice between serving Him and serving one’s parents, “choose ye to serve them”. Jesus rebuked those who did the reverse, declaring what they owed their parents Corban, a gift to God.

Parents’ pleasure is to be sought “on condition” that they do not bar the way to God. The Qur’an sets the same condition and the same courtesy: if they strive with thee to make thee ascribe partners unto Me, obey them not, yet consort with them in the world kindly.

Jesus puts the condition in its hardest form: if any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, he cannot be my disciple. What does the reading keep that this saying, taken alone, would lose?

The rights of parents are sacred “even should they perpetrate injustices against thee”. Confucius allowed a son to remonstrate, but gently, and with increased reverence, and should they punish him, he does not allow himself to murmur.

The reading speaks to a child wronged by a father. Lear speaks as a father wronged: how sharper than a serpent’s tooth it is to have a thankless child. He had first demanded that love be declared and measured. Whose injustice came first in that house, and does it matter to what each owes?
“Deal with him under all conditions with patience.” Proverbs asks it especially when the parent is weak: hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.

The son should “seek diligently to ensure the comfort and welfare” of his father. Confucius thought care without respect no better than what is given to animals: without reverence, what is there to distinguish the one support from the other?
Children’s prosperity “depends upon the good pleasure of parents”. Paul calls it the first commandment with promise: that it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.
“Thou must, therefore, please thy mother.” Proverbs counts what a child’s conduct does to each parent: a wise son maketh a glad father, but a foolish son is the heaviness of his mother.
The verse quoted in the letter: say not “Fie” unto them nor repulse them, but speak unto them a gracious word, and lower unto them the wing of submission.
Mothers have rights joined with the rights of the Lord. Ruth owed her husband’s mother nothing in law, and said: whither thou goest, I will go; thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God.
A son should forsake his own comfort for his parents’ ease. Joseph, grown great in Egypt, placed his father and his brethren in the best of the land and nourished his father with bread.
A daughter is praised for serving her mother. The Qur’an gives the reason children owe it: his mother beareth him with reluctance, and bringeth him forth with reluctance.

The training of children is “a great service”. Mencius would have the care of a household reach past it: treat with the kindness due to youth the young in your own family, so that the young in the families of others shall be similarly treated.

Obey your parents, the children are told, and “mirror forth the words of Christ”. Christ, told that his mother stood outside, asked: who is my mother? whosoever shall do the will of my Father, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother. Does the wider family replace the first, or rest on it?
“The child is the secret essence of its sire.” Wordsworth turns the proverb round: the Child is Father of the Man.
“Blessed is the one who arises to serve” in the prime of youth. The Preacher: remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not.
The Bible’s picture of a call heard young is the boy Samuel, woken three times in the night and taught to answer: speak, for thy servant heareth.
Youth is “characterised by strength and vigour”. John’s first letter addresses the young by that mark: I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong.

Youth is “the choice hour of human life”. The Preacher blesses it and adds a weight: rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment. Does his warning darken the springtime or give it its worth?
In youth “former conditions and needs are superseded”. Paul: when I became a man, I put away childish things.
The young are to be deepened in knowledge and to follow an example in their public addresses. Paul to his young colleague: let no man despise thy youth, but be thou an example of the believers.
The future “depends upon the energy and devotion of the rising generation”. Joel’s promise names them: your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your young men shall see visions.
The Báb was twenty-five when He declared His mission, and many of His first disciples younger. Jeremiah pleaded his age and was answered: say not, I am a child.

Youth’s vitality and adaptability “make them potent instruments”. Bacon weighed the same qualities and found a cost: young men are fitter to invent than to judge, fitter for execution than for counsel. How do the readings provide for the judgment he finds wanting?

shortfall: This guide places 46 outside quotations beside its 61. A dozen letters repeat the duty of pleasing one’s parents in nearly the same words, and the closing passages on Bahá’í youth and community plans speak of arrangements particular to that community; a companion is given where one could say something more.

ephesians-children-obey-your-parents.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; which is the first commandment with promise; That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth

proverbs-despise-not-thy-mother.text: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old

luke-about-my-fathers-business.text: And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing. And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business? And they understood not the saying which he spake unto them. And he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them

luke-hate-not-his-father.text: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple

ecclesiastes-rejoice-o-young-man.text: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thine heart, and in the sight of thine eyes: but know thou, that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment

john-epistle-young-men-because-ye-are-st.text: I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one

lamentations-yoke-in-his-youth.text: It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth

psalm-as-a-father-pitieth.text: Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him

samuel-lent-him-to-the-lord.text: For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: Therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord

samuel-child-samuel-speak.text: And the Lord called Samuel again the third time. And he arose and went to Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou didst call me. And Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child. Therefore Eli said unto Samuel, Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth

quran-if-they-strive-with-thee.text: But if they strive with thee to make thee ascribe unto Me as partner that of which thou hast no knowledge, then obey them not. Consort with them in the world kindly, and follow the path of him who repenteth unto Me. Then unto Me will be your return, and I shall tell you what ye used to do -

genesis-joseph-nourished-his-father.text: And Joseph placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded. And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his father's household, with bread, according to their families

gibran-your-children-are-not-your-childr.text: Your children are not your children. / They are the sons and daughters of Life's longing for itself. / They come through you but not from you, / And though they are with you yet they belong not to you
gibran-your-children-are-not-your-childr.author: Kahlil Gibran

analects-without-reverence.text: The filial piety nowadays means the support of one's parents. But dogs and horses likewise are able to do something in the way of support;-without reverence, what is there to distinguish the one support given from the other
analects-without-reverence.author: Confucius

analects-remonstrate-but-gently.text: In serving his parents, a son may remonstrate with them, but gently; when he sees that they do not incline to follow his advice, he shows an increased degree of reverence, but does not abandon his purpose; and should they punish him, he does not allow himself to murmur
analects-remonstrate-but-gently.author: Confucius

bacon-joys-of-parents-are-secret.text: The joys of parents are secret; and so are their griefs and fears. They cannot utter the one; nor they will not utter the other. Children sweeten labors; but they make misfortunes more bitter. They increase the cares of life; but they mitigate the remembrance of death
bacon-joys-of-parents-are-secret.author: Francis Bacon

bacon-young-men-fitter-to-invent.text: Young men are fitter to invent than to judge; fitter for execution than for counsel; and fitter for new projects than for settled business
bacon-young-men-fitter-to-invent.author: Francis Bacon
